{"findings": [
  {
    "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
    "line": 8,
    "severity": "critical",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Zod schema uses an object toString as a property key, so credential sharing validation always fails",
    "body": "In minimumTokenResponseSchema, the computed property `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` evaluates to a literal key like \"[object Object]\" and requires that exact property to exist. Real OAuth refresh responses do not contain such a key, so `safeParse(response)` will fail whenever APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and the sync endpoint is used, causing every affected integration to throw \"Invalid refreshed tokens were returned\". Use `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` or a proper passthrough schema instead of computed keys."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
    "line": 26,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "data",
    "title": "Missing refresh_token is replaced with a dummy string, corrupting stored credentials",
    "body": "The code assigns `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = \"refresh_token\"` whenever the token response omits that field. Many OAuth providers, like Microsoft, do not return a refresh token on refresh. Callers that merge `response.data` into their existing credential (for example Office 365) will overwrite the real refresh token with this invalid placeholder, causing subsequent refreshes to fail with invalid_grant. Preserve the existing refresh token instead of injecting a dummy value."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
    "line": 15,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Returns raw fetch Response, breaking callers that expect token data objects",
    "body": "When credential sharing is enabled, this function returns the raw `Response` from `fetch(CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT)` instead of parsing it into the shape that callers expect. Callers such as Google Calendar (`const token = res?.data;`), HubSpot (`await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` as a token object with `.expiresIn`), and Zoho apps (`tokenInfo.data`) assume either an object with a `.data` property or direct token fields. With a native `Response` those properties are undefined, causing TypeErrors or silently skipped refreshes. Define a single response contract and parse the response accordingly, or update every caller to handle the returned type."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
    "line": 97,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "data",
    "title": "Stores Zod safeParse result wrapper instead of parsed credential in the database",
    "body": "`const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` returns the entire `safeParse` result object (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), but that value is then saved as the credential key. This corrupts the persisted Google Calendar credential; the next load will fail when `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` receives this wrapper instead of the expected token object. Use the `.data` property of the parse result for the stored key."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
    "line": 96,
    "severity": "critical",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "prisma is used but not imported",
    "body": "The newly added code calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` in `getClient`, but this file has no `import prisma from \"@calcom/prisma\";` at the top. At runtime this will throw `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` whenever Salesforce credentials are refreshed. Add the missing import."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts",
    "line": 93,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Passes credentialId instead of userId to credential sync endpoint",
    "body": "In `refreshAccessToken`, the call to `refreshOAuthTokens` passes `credentialId` as the third argument, which is treated as the userId. That value is sent as `calcomUserId` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, so the self-hosted platform receives the internal Cal.com credential ID rather than the owning user's ID and cannot correctly sync the right user's credentials. Pass the actual user ID associated with the credential, such as `credential.userId`."
  },
  {
    "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
    "line": 77,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "data",
    "title": "Updating an existing credential does not clear the invalid flag",
    "body": "When the webhook updates an existing credential, it only replaces `key` but leaves any previous `invalid: true` value untouched. If a credential was marked invalid (for example after an invalid_grant error) and the self-hosted app store then pushes fresh valid keys, the credential remains invalid and continues to be ignored by the app. The update should set `invalid: false` when synced credentials are meant to reactivate the connection."
  }
]}

findings.title: Zod schema uses an object toString as a property key, so credential sharing validation always fails
findings.body: In minimumTokenResponseSchema, the computed property `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` evaluates to a literal key like "[object Object]" and requires that exact property to exist. Real OAuth refresh responses do not contain such a key, so `safeParse(response)` will fail whenever APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and the sync endpoint is used, causing every affected integration to throw "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` or a proper passthrough schema instead of computed keys.

findings.title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with a dummy string, corrupting stored credentials
findings.body: The code assigns `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` whenever the token response omits that field. Many OAuth providers, like Microsoft, do not return a refresh token on refresh. Callers that merge `response.data` into their existing credential (for example Office 365) will overwrite the real refresh token with this invalid placeholder, causing subsequent refreshes to fail with invalid_grant. Preserve the existing refresh token instead of injecting a dummy value.

findings.title: Returns raw fetch Response, breaking callers that expect token data objects
findings.body: When credential sharing is enabled, this function returns the raw `Response` from `fetch(CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT)` instead of parsing it into the shape that callers expect. Callers such as Google Calendar (`const token = res?.data;`), HubSpot (`await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` as a token object with `.expiresIn`), and Zoho apps (`tokenInfo.data`) assume either an object with a `.data` property or direct token fields. With a native `Response` those properties are undefined, causing TypeErrors or silently skipped refreshes. Define a single response contract and parse the response accordingly, or update every caller to handle the returned type.

findings.title: Stores Zod safeParse result wrapper instead of parsed credential in the database
findings.body: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` returns the entire `safeParse` result object (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), but that value is then saved as the credential key. This corrupts the persisted Google Calendar credential; the next load will fail when `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` receives this wrapper instead of the expected token object. Use the `.data` property of the parse result for the stored key.

findings.title: prisma is used but not imported
findings.body: The newly added code calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` in `getClient`, but this file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";` at the top. At runtime this will throw `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` whenever Salesforce credentials are refreshed. Add the missing import.

findings.title: Passes credentialId instead of userId to credential sync endpoint
findings.body: In `refreshAccessToken`, the call to `refreshOAuthTokens` passes `credentialId` as the third argument, which is treated as the userId. That value is sent as `calcomUserId` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, so the self-hosted platform receives the internal Cal.com credential ID rather than the owning user's ID and cannot correctly sync the right user's credentials. Pass the actual user ID associated with the credential, such as `credential.userId`.

findings.title: Updating an existing credential does not clear the invalid flag
findings.body: When the webhook updates an existing credential, it only replaces `key` but leaves any previous `invalid: true` value untouched. If a credential was marked invalid (for example after an invalid_grant error) and the self-hosted app store then pushes fresh valid keys, the credential remains invalid and continues to be ignored by the app. The update should set `invalid: false` when synced credentials are meant to reactivate the connection.
